title: Ninth stale-suite triage draw. Eleven of the twenty files the item names already carried a verdict, so the genuinely untriaged half is the fourteen operator-integration suites, and the one directory this draw can wire is wired because an earlier item's hold is discharged

filingCorrection.claim: The item is filed as 'the next 20 stale suites to triage ... excluding every directory already gated'. Eleven of the twenty already carry an explicit verdict in a repo-owned triage record, each with a named owning item, recorded between 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-26 — before this item was filed.
filingCorrection.measuredHow: node scripts/quality/triage-record-census-reconciliation.mjs on this base, intersected against the twenty paths the item names. Not reasoned from the item's text.
filingCorrection.note: The eleven are exactly the eleven the item describes as carrying a governed-risk band at ranks 1-7. The nine it drew from rank 9 are operator-integration files, and those nine plus the five it named as not-drawn are the only genuinely untriaged work in the draw. So the ranked, governed-risk half of this draw was entirely re-offered work.
filingCorrection.whyTheDrawCouldNotKnow: governedRiskRanking's sole input is untriagedUnrunTestFiles, and that predicate is `!covered && !declaredQuarantine` (scripts/quality/test-ci-coverage-census.mjs). It does not consult triage records at all. A file with a written verdict, a recorded reason and a named owner is still counted untriaged and is still ranked, so the ranking keeps offering judged work. T-615 fixed the narrow case of this — a file declared in scripts/quality/*-quarantine.json — and the general case is untouched.

censusBlindSpot.subject: Every triage verdict is invisible to the instrument the triage ranking is drawn from.
censusBlindSpot.andDoesNotGate: It exits 0 whatever it finds, so nothing objects when the ranking re-offers verdicted work. Three consecutive draws — T-492, T-493 and this one — have re-drawn already-judged files, and this is the mechanism.

measuredAfterThisChange.note: This change moves the verdicted-but-ranked count from 68 to 81. Triaging a file writes a verdict and does not remove it from the ranking, so the 14 operator-integration files judged here joined that set and only the one wired file left it. Doing the work the item asked for made the number worse by 13, which is the sharpest available statement of the defect: the instrument the ranking is drawn from cannot see the work done to it. Re-measured at the merged base; the figures at the original base were 71 of 304 and 84 of 303, the same +13.

scope.drawnFrom: The twenty paths T-771 names individually, plus the five operator-integration siblings it names as not-drawn, because the wiring unit is the directory and a directory cannot be judged from nine of its fourteen files.
scope.everyFileWasExecuted: Each of the 25 was run on its own with npx jest --runTestsByPath on this base. Counts below are the count of suites RUN, never a count read from the census: the census says 'not reached by CI', which is not the same claim as 'fails'.

wiring.namedAsADirectory: Named as a DIRECTORY without a trailing slash, per that workflow's header, and its line leaves src/__tests__/behaviors/product-directory-ci-coverage.baseline.json in the same change, which the ratchet asserts as set equality in both directions.
wiring.provenBy: src/__tests__/behaviors/t771-nda-suite-wiring.test.ts, which answers through the census's own resolver rather than by grepping the workflow for a string, and which fails if the directory is re-added to the dark baseline or if the suite's exhaustive expectation is narrowed.
wiring.whyOnlyOne: Of the eight directories this draw touches, seven cannot be wired on this item's evidence. Six are partially covered, so wiring the directory would sweep in siblings this draw did not judge — the acceptance forbids it. The seventh, src/__tests__/integration/ops, is fully unrun and therefore decidable here, and is withheld for the two reasons recorded under heldDirectories.

dischargedHold.reasonAsRecorded: Measured red there: 1 of 4 failing, because the repository had gained a signature-evidence field group that the exhaustive expectation did not carry. T-472 explicitly forbade repairing it in place and assigned the widening to T-519, with the instruction not to switch toEqual to toMatchObject because that would delete the exhaustiveness the test exists for.
dischargeEvidence: Re-measured on this base: 4 of 4 green, 0 failing.

T-519 landed the widening in bd63332ea4 (#8183), 'assert NDA signature evidence instead of ignoring it'. The expectation is still a toEqual and now carries the whole signatureEvidence group, with an in-file comment recording that toMatchObject was rejected on purpose. The hold was discharged by widening, not by weakening.

The subject has two non-test importers on live product paths — src/lib/source/rfx-delivery/source-backed-preview.ts and src/lib/source/new-workspace/stage05-nda-coverage.ts — so wiring covers code a product path reaches rather than adding a number to the census.
dischargedHold.whatWasLeftUndone: T-519 discharged the reason and did not wire the suite, so it has sat dark since, still on the dark baseline and still counted untriaged. The rule this violates is already written in src/__tests__/behaviors/t754-credited-suite-wiring.test.ts: a discharged reason should be wired in the change that discharges it. Wiring it here is the close, not a new judgement.

src/__tests__/integration/ops.reasonNotWired: Two of the fourteen are red, and five of the fourteen carry a source-text scanner. Either alone forbids wiring the directory. The acceptance forbids file-by-file wiring, so the twelve green suites stay dark until the scanner blocks are separated and the two reds are settled.
src/__tests__/integration/ops.machineEnforcedSince: T-770 merged a control that refuses any workflow jest command reaching a declared source-text scanner by exact path OR by any ancestor directory under src/. The five scanner declarations in this record put src/__tests__/integration/ops behind that control, so this reason is now executable rather than narrated.

partiallyCoveredDirectories.reasonNotWired: Wiring one of these as a directory reaches siblings this draw did not judge, and two of the six hold a file another open item owns. The acceptance names this case and forbids it.

forbiddenEdits: This record judges 25 files and edits none of them. The only test file this change writes is its own control, src/__tests__/behaviors/t771-nda-suite-wiring.test.ts, which is not among the judged paths. A triage that repairs its own subject and reports the repair as a finding is the shape this family exists against.

followOnItems.why: The census's untriaged predicate ignores triage records, so 71 of 304 files carry a verdict and are ranked anyway. The reconciliation script measures it and exits 0.

Twelve of the fourteen operator-integration suites are green and hold 286 cases; five of the fourteen confine a source-text scanner to part of the file and two are red. Separating those blocks and settling the two reds is what makes the directory wireable.

suites.rationale: Green, 10 cases, and not a scanner: its own header records that it used to read six route files with readFileSync and was rewritten to render instead, so the one readFileSync match in it is that sentence. Already verdicted wire_into_ci by T-556 and owned by T-557. Its directory is partially covered, so this draw cannot wire it without reaching four siblings it did not judge.

Red 2 of 7, and both failures are byte assertions over a component's source: one expects a display string that a refactor moved into a sibling language module, the other expects a useState initialiser written verbatim. Neither indicates a defect in the product. Already verdicted rewrite_as_behavior by T-479 and owned by T-481.

Green, but green on byte assertions over source read through the same helper as its red sibling, so it is a scanner that has not yet been overtaken by a refactor rather than a behavioural suite. Already verdicted rewrite_as_behavior by T-479 and owned by T-481.

A control-plane literal-leak prohibition: it scans src/lib, src/app and src/components for a fixture tenant's display strings and requires zero. It is RED against five real occurrences across three modules — two in a Programs UI type module and three in two Intelligence ask modules — so this is a live governance violation and not a stale expectation. textIsTheSubject is true: the prohibition is about the bytes of the tree, and there is no run of the product that can answer it. Already verdicted repair by T-556 and owned by T-560; the five occurrences are what that item has to clear. Named here as counts and module paths, never as the strings themselves, because this record is public.

Green, 10 cases, behavioural. Already verdicted wire_into_ci by T-556 and owned by T-557. Its directory holds the red purity scanner above, so a directory sweep here would wire a red suite another item owns.

Green on its own, and held twice over: verdicted repair by T-475 and owned by T-755, and named in the quarantine list of src/__tests__/behaviors/source-contract-suite-ci-coverage.test.ts, a control that runs today and asserts no jest command in unit-suites.yml mentions it. Wiring it would turn that control red.

Verdicted wire_into_ci by T-475 and then deliberately WITHHELD by T-754 with a written reason — its fixture carries no register contract identity, so it cannot reproduce the live identity split — and quarantined by the sibling behaviours control. T-754's own file asserts that this quarantine is still in place, so wiring it fails two controls, not one.

Verdicted wire_into_ci by T-475 and withheld by T-754 because the module under test has no non-test importer, so running it would add a number to the census without covering code any product path reaches. T-754 re-measures that reason every run and fails if the module gains a runtime caller.
Same hold as its sibling above, with the same executable reason: no non-test importer, re-measured by T-754's control rather than narrated.

Red 3 of 3. Already verdicted update_with_reason_recorded by T-475 and owned by T-757, and T-754's control records why it is NOT discharged where its two directory siblings were: its dataset roots were deleted rather than renamed, so retiring the module versus re-wiring it is a decision rather than a re-baseline.

The one row in this draw whose earlier hold is DISCHARGED. T-472 measured it red 1 of 4 and assigned the widening to T-519, which landed it in bd63332ea4 (#8183) by extending the exhaustive toEqual to carry the signature-evidence group, explicitly refusing toMatchObject. Re-measured here: 4 of 4 green. The suite asserts tenant, event and declared-supplier scoping on the read and fails closed on an unavailable register, and its subject has two non-test importers on live product paths. Not a scanner. Its directory is 1 of 1 unrun, so the directory is decided by this draw alone and is wired here.

suites.scannerScope: one describe block, an import prohibition over the module's own source with comments stripped; the other cases are behavioural over the parsed read model
suites.rationale: Red 22 of 32 on ONE cause, and the cause is the seed, not the module: docs/build/agent-dispatch-queue.json declares its own lifecycle as proposed, ready, blocked, in_progress, complete — and all 20 of its items carry the status merged, which is in neither that array nor the module's alias table, so normalizeState throws and takes every case that loads the file. The module's aliases mirror the file's declared lifecycle exactly, so the module agrees with the file's contract and the file's own rows do not. Both arrive in the SAME single commit, 5d795a3976 (#2514), so the pair shipped disagreeing and this suite has never passed; nothing ran it to say so. Repair is on the seed or on a deliberate widening of the lifecycle, and it is a judgement about ops vocabulary rather than a re-baseline, so it is not taken here — a triage may not edit a file it judges.

Green, 27 cases, behavioural — it builds retrospective models and asserts the returned shape. Wireable on its own merits and held only by its directory: five siblings carry a source-text scanner and two are red, and the acceptance forbids wiring this directory file by file.

Red 8 of 61, and not a scanner: every read is JSON.parse of a committed data artifact and every assertion is over the parsed model, which is a data contract rather than a byte assertion. The eight failures are expectations pinned to a moment: an exact lastUpdated string, an exact count of 33 waves against 40 today, and a required field spelled name where the data spells it title. Pinning a mutable lastUpdated stamp is the defect — the same assertion cannot survive the next write to the file it guards — so the repair is to assert the field's shape and monotonicity rather than its value, and to derive the wave set rather than count it.
Green, 45 cases, the largest clean suite in the directory. Behavioural throughout. Held by the directory for the reason above.

Green, 12 cases. It reads files, and none of the reads is a source-text assertion: it parses its own JSON fixtures and compares a fixture's bytes before and after to prove the helper did not mutate committed input. That is a behavioural claim about the subject, asserted through bytes rather than about them.

suites.scannerScope: eight cases, each re-reading the validator script's own source and asserting a substring of it
suites.rationale: Green today and a source-text scanner, so the inherited rule refuses to wire it. The subject is an executable script: its behaviour is reachable by running it over fixtures, which is what the rewrite should assert, and the eight substring cases should be deleted rather than sharpened.

suites.scannerScope: one case, a static check that the python script imports only stdlib and makes no network call, parsed out of its source lines
suites.rationale: Ten of its eleven cases execute the script and assert its output and its non-mutation of the manifest; one reads the script's source and asserts its import set. The prohibition is real but the instrument is wrong for a script that can be run: a dependency check belongs in a lint rule or a packaging check, not in a jest byte scan. Separating that one case is what frees this file.

suites.scannerScope: the larger share of its cases, each re-reading a shell script's source and asserting on the code with comments stripped
suites.rationale: Green, 19 cases, and the heaviest scanner in the directory by read count. Its subject is a shell script that can be executed against fixtures, so the questions it asks about the script's text are answerable by running it. Rewrite rather than sharpen.

Green, 8 cases, and its single file read is a sha256 over a temp report written by the test itself, used to prove the validator does not rewrite its input. Not a source-text scanner: nothing in it asserts over the bytes of a repository file.

suites.rationale: Green, 44 cases, no file reads at all — the largest clean suite in the directory and the cheapest coverage in this draw. Held only by its siblings.

suites.rationale: Green, 37 cases, no file reads. Held only by its siblings.

suites.rationale: Green, 28 cases, no file reads. Guards a control that matters to every agent on this repository — the shared stash stack — and it runs nowhere.

suites.scannerScope: one read of the report script's own source
suites.rationale: Green, 12 cases, mostly executing the script over a temp tree. One read asserts over the script's source, which is enough to make it a declared scanner and enough to keep the directory behind T-770's refusal. The subject is runnable, so the rewrite is cheap.

idBandNote: Follow-on ids were filed as T-773 and T-774, not T-772. T-772 was drafted here and then taken by a sibling watcher run at 19:15Z while this item was in flight, which is the collision the id-band rule exists for and which no control detects. Re-measured free in the backlog and the register at 19:26Z before renumbering.

rebasedOnto.how: A real merge commit of origin/main into the branch. No rebase, no force-push. The only conflict was this repository's generated coverage census snapshot, resolved by regenerating it from the merged tree rather than by hand-merging a generated file; the dark-directory baseline auto-merged as a union of two removals, which is correct because each side wired a different directory.
rebasedOnto.everyFigureReMeasured: Nothing is carried forward. All 25 suites were re-run individually at the new base: 20 green, 5 red, every per-suite count identical. The 11-of-20 already-verdicted finding reproduces id for id, record for record, owner for owner.

reconciliationAtNewBase.delta: +13, the same direction and magnitude measured at the original base
